reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly supports the role of lattice misfit at interfaces in impeding dislocations and affecting creep resistance, including the non-monotonic relationship and the benefit of moderate negative misfit. However, the evidence is from high-entropy superalloys (HESAs) with γ/γ′ interfaces, not from deliberately engineered multilayer coatings, so the extrapolation to alternating HEA layers with controlled misfits is a gap. The diffusion barrier premise is mentioned in E2 but not specifically tied to misfit-engineered multilayers.
premises: Engineered layering with controlled lattice misfits at interfaces acts as effective barriers to dislocation motion
Interfacial regions inhibit atomic diffusion, retarding creep deformation
Moderate negative lattice misfit enhances interfacial coherency and stabilizes microstructure, improving creep resistance
Excessively large misfit increases interfacial strain energy and deteriorates performance
Multilayer interfaces with misfit generate local strain fields that impede dislocation nucleation and propagation
